task_row_model.query: In Python, what is the difference between a shallow copy and a deep copy for lists and nested objects, and when should I use copy.copy versus copy.deepcopy? Include brief examples and when each is appropriate.

documents.content: In JavaScript, arrays and objects are copied by reference by default. A common way to make a shallow copy of an array is using slice(0) or the spread operator [...arr], which copies the top-level elements but retains references for nested objects. For example, copying an array of objects will duplicate the container but not the inner object references. For deep cloning in JS you can use structuredClone or third-party libraries like lodash.cloneDeep for complex nested structures that need full duplication.

The Python copy module provides two helpers: copy.copy(obj) and copy.deepcopy(obj). copy.copy performs a shallow copy: it constructs a new container and inserts references to the same contained objects. copy.deepcopy attempts to recursively copy all objects found in the original, producing independent nested copies. For user-defined classes, __deepcopy__ can be implemented to control deep-copy behavior. deepcopy is generally slower and may require special handling for objects with external resources or shared state.

Shallow vs deep copy: a shallow copy copies the outer container but not nested mutable objects; a deep copy recursively duplicates nested objects so changes to the copy don't affect the original. Example: a = [[1], [2]]; b = a[:] or b = list(a) or b = copy.copy(a) produces a shallow copy: b[0] is a[0]. Modifying b[0].append(3) also changes a. Using import copy; c = copy.deepcopy(a) creates independent nested lists so modifying c does not touch a. Use shallow copies when you only need a new top-level container and nested items shouldn't be mutated separately; use deepcopy when you will modify nested mutable objects and need full isolation. Note deepcopy can be slower and may require custom __deepcopy__ for complex classes.

A shallow copy creates a new object but inserts references to the same child objects; copy.copy implements this for many built-in containers and user-defined objects. deepcopy walks the object graph and creates new instances for contained objects; this is usually implemented by copy.deepcopy and respects __deepcopy__ hooks on classes. deepcopy can avoid shared mutable state but is more expensive. For classes that manage external handles or rely on identity, you often need to implement custom copying logic to avoid duplicating resources or violating invariants.

Cloning a repository with git clone duplicates a remote repository locally. This operation copies commits, refs, branches and tags to a new directory; it does not duplicate working tree state beyond checking out the default branch. If you want to copy a project structure without history, you can use git archive or create a new repository and copy files. Git operations are about version history and metadata, not in-memory object duplication used in programming languages.
